account: The dossier provides the formula and objective but no worked derivation or endpoint table. I re-derived the z-interval bounds from the equation using exact rational inequalities, and produced a full 33-row endpoint table via exact rational arithmetic. The lower bound is y (from z >= y) and floor(1/R)+1 (from positive integer w), and the upper bound is floor(2/R) (from w >= z). All endpoints match the separator facts. However, I have not verified the table against an independent source, and the dossier contains no explicit complete enumeration of solutions, so I cannot yet assert the final count.
assumptions: All six feasible x values in 3..8 are positive, and the feasible y-intervals from the separator facts are complete.
The count of 33 feasible pairs matches the union of the given y-intervals.

In the upper-bound derivation, when 1/R and 2/R are integers, the strict inequalities z > 1/R and z < 2/R become z >= floor(1/R)+1 and z <= floor(2/R)-?; the formula's stated floor(2/R) is interpreted as the maximum integer strictly less than 2/R, which equals floor(2/R) unless 2/R is an integer, in which case it is 2/R - 1; the endpoint table reflects that convention.

claims.statement: For R > 0, the equation 1/x + 1/y + 1/z + 1/w = 1/2 implies 1/z + 1/w = R.

Given R > 0 and positive integers z <= w, the equation 1/z + 1/w = R implies R < 1/z + 1/z = 2/z, hence z < 2/R, so z <= floor(2/R) when 2/R is not an integer, and z <= 2/R - 1 = floor(2/R) otherwise (with adaptations when 2/R is integer).
The upper bound z <= floor(2/R) follows from z <= w and 1/z + 1/w = R, because 1/z + 1/w <= 2/z implies z <= 2/R; since z is an integer, z <= floor(2/R).

The lower bound floor(1/R)+1 <= z follows from w >= z and 1/z + 1/w = R: since 1/z + 1/w <= 1/z + 1/z = 2/z, that gives an upper bound, but the lower bound comes from w >= z giving 1/w <= 1/z, so R <= 2/z, which would give z <= 2/R; the lower bound floor(1/R)+1 arises because R = 1/z + 1/w > 1/z (since w finite positive), so z > 1/R, and as an integer z >= floor(1/R)+1.
The lower bound z >= y holds directly from the problem constraint y <= z.
The integrality test w = z/(R*z - 1) follows from the equation: R = 1/z + 1/w implies (R - 1/z) = 1/w, so w = 1/(R - 1/z) = z/(R*z - 1).
No integer solution can lie outside the interval [max(y, floor(1/R)+1), floor(2/R)] because any solution must satisfy z >= y, z > 1/R, and z <= 2/R; these combine to the stated bounds.
